description: Which states received a systematic month-by-month sweep for a given window, so that a state with no rows in that window can be distinguished from a state nobody looked at. Without this, the two are indistinguishable from the inventory alone. `windows` lists systematic month-by-month sweeps, where absence is a finding; `discovery_passes` lists statewide discovery searches, which raise coverage but where absence is only suggestive.

windows.method: Month-by-month agentic sweep of each state (one research pass per state per month) covering moratorium votes, zoning hearings, legislative action, opposition activity, developer filings, litigation, and utility/grid proceedings. Events were parsed deterministically and converted to inventory candidates only on evidence.

notes.AZ: No local development moratorium found in any Arizona city or county. The only qualifying statewide action was HB 4168 s.31, a freeze on new applications to the state data-center tax relief program, which is out of scope for this inventory and is recorded in state_legislation.csv instead.
notes.coverage_effect: Conversion of a state's sweep can change its count substantially. Florida held 1 inventory row before its sweep and 14 after; Georgia went from 26 to 47; South Carolina from 1 to 6; Utah from 0 to 6. None of these states changed in the world; only our looking did.
notes.completion: The sweep now covers all 50 states for this window. Ten states recorded no local adoption during it: Alaska, Arizona, Delaware, Hawaii, Idaho, Louisiana, Rhode Island, Vermont, West Virginia, and Wyoming. Wyoming is the sharpest case - Cheyenne's proposed 12-month moratorium was rejected 9-1 on second reading, so the absence is a decision rather than a gap.

windows.field_note: swept_states_with_no_adoptions_in_window means no local instrument was ADOPTED during this window. It does not mean the state has no moratoria at all: Idaho, for example, carries a 2025 Kootenai County instrument in the inventory but adopted nothing new between 2026-05-01 and 2026-07-31.
windows.correction_2026_09_23: The v2026.07 list named ten states: AK, AZ, DE, HI, ID, LA, RI, VT, WV, WY. The 2026-09-23 search and QA found May-July adoptions the sweep missed in Idaho (Elmore County 2026-07-02, Bannock County 2026-07-30), Louisiana (Iberville Parish 2026-07-15) and Rhode Island (Westerly 2026-07-27), and showed New Hampshire's only instrument (Nottingham) was ratified 2026-09-08, outside the window. The sweep also missed 161 adoptions inside the window in states it did cover, mostly Ohio and Michigan townships, so counts for this window are lower bounds too.

unswept_caveat: All 50 states were swept for the 2026-05-01/2026-07-31 window, so counts in it are no longer coverage-limited. Earlier windows were not swept this way; treat pre-2026-05 counts as lower bounds.

discovery_passes.method: Statewide discovery search per state (not month by month): one research agent per state or state group ran sector-by-sector web searches (Exa + Google, fused) for data center, battery storage, solar, wind and cryptocurrency-mining moratoria adopted, extended or proposed since roughly 2026-08-01, read statewide roundups including their embedded map data, fetched primary instruments where available, and archived every cited source. Every worklist row was also rechecked (Process A). See work/research-process.md.
discovery_passes.field_note: This window is a discovery search, weaker than the May-July month-by-month sweep: absence of a new instrument in a state is suggestive, not a finding. HI, WV and WY have no local instrument in the inventory at all as of 2026-09-23.
